predecessors.name: Yuan dynasty
predecessors.text: eastern Hubei around Qishui/Qizhou, taken from the Yuan in 1351

successors.name: Chen Han
successors.text: 'He subsequently declared himself emperor of the Great Han' and took most Tianwan territories (Chen Han page); Hubei, Hunan and Jiangxi

successors.name: Ming Xia
successors.text: Sichuan, held by Ming Yuzhen since 1357 in Xu Shouhui's name and declared the kingdom of Longshu

ledger.x: 1351: Zou Pusheng takes Qishui in southern Hubei and enthrones Xu Shouhui as emperor of Tianwan.
1352: Tianwan reaches Jiujiang and takes Nanchang and Changsha.
1353: Toqto'a's army takes the Tianwan capital.
1353: the Yangtze and Jiangxi cities are lost with the capital.
Winter 1355/56: Xu Shouhui moves the court to Hanyang.
1357: Tianwan's general Chen Youliang takes Jiangxi.
1357: Ming Yuzhen conquers Sichuan in Xu Shouhui's name.
1360: Ming Yuzhen takes the title of king of Longshu in Sichuan after Xu's murder.
June 1360: Chen Youliang murders Xu Shouhui at Hanyang and takes Tianwan's land.

wars.name: Toqto'a's campaign against Tianwan
wars.outcome: Yuan victory: Qishui taken in the autumn of 1353, Xu escapes to the Huangmei mountains; Ni Wenjun's fleet retakes Hanyang in January 1355.

wars.name: Red Turban Rebellions
wars.outcome: The Yuan loses the Yangtze valley and the Huai to rebel states; Zhu Yuanzhang absorbs most of them and proclaims the Ming in 1368.

certainty.note: A rebel regime holding river cities; the pages name cities and circuits, never a frontier.
